stem: 'At least one' is best counted as?
candidateDistractors: When the constraint forces disjoint sub-situations
trapHints: 'At least one' = total − none (don't sum cases): For 'at least one X', count the complement: \(\text{total}-(\text{none of X})\). Summing the cases 'exactly 1, exactly 2, …' is slower and easy to miscount. E.g. at least one typist when choosing 5 from 6 programmers + 4 typists is \(^{10}C_5-\,^6C_5=252-6=246\), not a sum of four separate terms.

trapHints: Collinear points form no triangle — subtract \(^kC_3\): \(^nC_3\) counts triangles only if no three points are collinear. If \(k\) of the points lie on one line, those \(^kC_3\) triples are degenerate (no triangle), so the answer is \(^nC_3-\,^kC_3\). Likewise the diagonal formula \(\dfrac{n(n-3)}{2}=\,^nC_2-n\) subtracts the \(n\) sides from all \(^nC_2\) point-pairs.
